name: Gray-bellied Tesia
rangeDescription: Nepal to southern china (western yunnan and guangxi), southeastern asia, and java
description: Long-legged and short-tailed, this tiny bird moves rapidly and unseen through dark, dense undergrowth like a pint-sized shadow. Yellowish-green above and gray below, with a black line extending through the eye below a pale yellowish eyebrow.

name: Eastern Kingbird
rangeDescription: Eastern north america; winters mainly western amazon basin
description: Fairly large flycatcher, dark gray above and clean white below with blacker head. Look for white tail tip.

name: Austral Negrito
rangeDescription: Central chile and argentina to tierra del fuego; winters to southeastern brazil
description: Tiny little terrestrial flycatcher, common in open habitats of southern South America in summer, migrates north in winter. Feeds mainly by hopping on the ground, but perches readily on posts, fences, and low bushes.

name: Bornean Stubtail
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern borneo (kinabalu to liang kubung)
description: Minute, ground-dwelling warbler of Borneo’s central mountain ranges. Scurries about like a rodent in the undergrowth, where it can be difficult to see well; note bright orangish brow stripe, brown back, and gray sides.

name: Rennell Fantail
rangeDescription: Forest of rennell (southeastern solomon islands)
description: Mostly mouse-brown with a slightly paler throat and a russet wingbar. Long tail, often fanned, has pale fringes.

name: Bronzy Jacamar
rangeDescription: Central amazonia, from eastern colombia and southern venezuela eastward to the guianas, southward to southeastern peru (madre de dios), northern bolivia, and south-central amazonian brazil (south to mato grosso)
description: Small, active, and locally distributed. Key field mark is overall bronzy color, which is evident in good light but hard to see otherwise.

name: Reichenow's Seedeater
rangeDescription: Djibouti, ethiopia, southeastern south sudan, southern somalia, northeastern uganda, kenya, and tanzania
description: A gray-brown seedeater with a complex brown-and-white facial pattern and a yellow rump that is conspicuous in flight. Found in savanna, woodland, and cultivated areas, usually in small flocks.

name: Purplish-backed Jay
rangeDescription: Lowlands of western mexico (southeastern sonora and chihuahua to nayarit)
description: Handsome, rather large jay. Common in tropical forest and woodland of northwest Mexico where it is endemic.

name: Bare-necked Fruitcrow
rangeDescription: Southern venezuela and the guianas to northern bolivia and amazonian brazil
description: Unusual medium-sized bird of forest canopy in Amazonia. Dark blue overall with bare, wrinkly blue skin on the neck and a pale bill.

name: Gray-and-gold Tanager
rangeDescription: Humid foothills of eastern panama to northwestern ecuador (pichincha)
description: Chunky medium-sized tanager found in the canopy of lowland and foothill forest from extreme eastern Panama to northwest Ecuador. Unmistakable in range: pale silvery-gray overall with a black face, a black shoulder, and messy black and gold spotting on the breast and nape.

name: Iranian Ground-Jay
rangeDescription: Desert steppes of central and eastern iran
description: Strange brownish corvid restricted to eastern Iran. Pinkish-buff overall, with a slightly decurved bill and black-and-white wing coverts.

name: Rufous-winged Illadopsis
rangeDescription: Senegal to ghana; single record from togo
description: A mid-sized, chunky, drably colored babbler. Has a white throat and pale gray underparts, often with some darker olive-brown on the breast.

name: Blackish Chat-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Andes of western venezuela (mérida, western barinas, and táchira)
description: Small flycatcher endemic to the Venezuela Andes. Plumage is entirely slate gray except for its conspicuous white eyebrows, which can shine like headlights in the gloom.
imageCreditName: Jhonathan Miranda - Wandering Venezuela Birding Expeditions

name: Blue Crane
rangeDescription: Locally in northern namibia, southern zimbabwe and south africa
description: A small, elegant, uniformly blue-gray crane that dwells in open habitats in pairs and variably sized groups. The bulbous head, plain face lacking any naked skin, and lack of contrast in the wings are distinctive.

name: Yellow-cheeked Lorikeet
rangeDescription: Montane forest of sulawesi
description: Small bright green lorikeet with bright yellow cheeks. Also note olive-yellow crown, yellow-edged “scaling” on the belly, and bright red bill.

name: Fiji White-eye
rangeDescription: Fiji (viti levu, ovalau, gau, vanua levu, taveuni, and kadavu)
description: A small, mostly citrine-yellow bird with a pale buffy-gray belly, a bold white eye-ring, and a black line from eye to bill. Bill dark.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Marañon Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: West slope of the andes of southwestern ecuador (loja) and northwestern peru (piura and cajamarca), and the arid tropical marañón valley in far southern ecuador and northern peru
description: Small, drab flycatcher with a limited range in southern Ecuador and northern Peru. It is mostly gray and brown, and may show faint yellow on the belly.

name: Colombian Chachalaca
rangeDescription: Northern and central colombia
description: Large chickenlike bird. Restricted to central Colombia; the only chachalaca in its limited range.

name: Splendid Sunbird
rangeDescription: Senegal to sierra leone, eastward to southern nigeria, cameroon, central african republic, northeastern democratic republic of the congo, and southwestern south sudan; nonbreeding visitor to northeastern gabon
description: A fairly large, long-billed sunbird in which males and females are very different. Males are dark, with an iridescent multi-colored hood and a black belly.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Golden-winged Cacique
rangeDescription: Southeastern bolivia (southern santa cruz to tarija) to paraguay, southern brazil, uruguay, and northeastern argentina
description: Black-and-yellow cacique found in humid forests, montane forests, and second growth. Mostly black with a bright yellow rump and large yellow patch on the inner wing.
